how: Kept by hand. The berths and their size limits are from each marina's own website, Go To Bermuda and the Superyacht Services Guide, read on 22 Nov 2026. The yearly figure is from the Bermuda Tourism Authority's quarterly report as Bernews published it. Recent visits are not kept here: superyachts_collect in run.py reads them each day from the Bernews super yacht stories and saves them in superyachts_news.json. No free source lists which yachts are in port right now, so the page links to the VesselFinder port pages for that.
intro: Bermuda is the mid Atlantic stop for yachts crossing between the Caribbean and Europe or New England. The busy months are April, May and June, with a smaller run south in the autumn.
stat: 107 superyacht calls in the first nine months of 2026, up 32% on the year before (Bermuda Tourism Authority).

berths.name: St George's Superyacht Dock
berths.note: The closest berth to the open Atlantic, minutes from the Town Cut. The best place on the island to see the biggest ones.

berths.name: Princess Marina
berths.where: Hamilton Princess, Pitts Bay Road, Hamilton
berths.note: The hotel marina. Walk the waterfront path or have a drink on the dock to see who is in.

berths.name: Royal Bermuda Yacht Club
berths.note: Home of the Newport Bermuda Race finish every other June.

berths.name: Powder Hole anchorage
berths.where: St George's Harbour, off Ordnance Island
berths.note: Where yachts wait or stay when the dock is full. Easy to see from the town waterfront.
